concerns.message: The panels lane doesn't own src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx, and that file decides what data each section component gets. ControllerSections receives only `scope` and `renderResult` (NodeDetail.tsx:260, ControllerSections.tsx:28). It gets no inputs, events, timeline, node or clock. ChallengeSections receives only `inputs` (NodeDetail.tsx:245). ReviewSections gets inputs and node but no timeline or clock. Yet the controller-panels scenario needs: the handoff wait (`inputs.workers[].receipt.native_started_at`/`launch_requested_at` → freeze or `stop.confirmed_at`), the approval `≈` instant (the integrate event's time, from events/timeline), and the branch and commit that integrate fast-forwarded (events or `inputs.source_branch`). The challenge headline's `11m07s over 3 attempts` needs the first attempt's start, which is in the timeline, not in `inputs.challenge` (that has only attempt, attempts and decided_at). The PRD's section index chips (`[Blocking 1] [Findings 4]`, `[Concerns 8] [Alternative & experiment]`) are built in NodeDetail's `sections` array (lines 170-179), which the lane also can't edit.
concerns.consequence: The worker has three ways out and all are bad. (1) It edits NodeDetail.tsx, and the verifier's ownership check rejects the snapshot. (2) It calls fetchEvents, fetchRunInputs, buildTimeline and useNow a second time inside the section components. That duplicates RunView's polling, ignores refreshToken and breaks the 'one useNow at RunView' rule (PRD 5.3), which is rework for S7. (3) It stops at `blocked` because controller-panels can't be met. Either way the lane is likely to need a rework round.

concerns.message: Both lanes' fixtures are added to PROJECT through fixtures/index.ts, so in the combined candidate Runs home lists the panels lane's runs too. The manual run awaiting approval (attention `approval`) lands in Needs you, and the running native review lands in Running. The lists lane writes runs-home in a worktree where ux-review.ts is still empty. Any assertion there on section counts (`Needs you · N`, `Running · N`, 'nothing is running') or on the exact contents of Recent passes in the lists snapshot and fails on the combined candidate. The same is true of lists changes to the CommandBlock/NowBanner DOM that the panels tests' node-next command assertions read.
concerns.consequence: The combined candidate check fails after both workers finish, and one lane needs another attempt. To avoid it: the lists lane scopes runs-home assertions to its own run ids (never whole-section counts), and the panels lane asserts command text with toContainText on `node-next`, not on CommandBlock's internal structure.

concerns.message: The running-reviewer line (`working 3m · deadline 11:10 (56m left)`) depends on the wall clock. Fixture `launched_at` values are fixed timestamps, so at real test time the deadline is months past. The PRD gives no wording for a passed deadline.
concerns.consequence: The assertion either flakes or the worker invents a wording such as 'overdue'. Without a page.clock (ux-time.spec.ts:38/99 already sets one) or seed times relative to now, the `≈ deadline` text differs between the worker and candidate phases.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Before launch, add src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx, and if needed src/projects/node/model.ts, to the panels lane's owned paths. The lists lane doesn't own either file, so the lanes stay file-disjoint. NodeDetail then passes what it already holds (`inputs`, `nodeEvents`, `timeline`, `clock`, `node`, `now`) to ChallengeSections and ControllerSections, and adds the review and challenge section-index entries. The headline, wait, approval and deadline wording go in pure helpers in node/panels.ts that take those values, so no section fetches or ticks on its own.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Spend about 10 minutes, before any worker starts, writing typed stubs in node/panels.ts for `handoffWait(inputs, events)`, `approvalInstant(timeline)`, `integrateLine(inputs, events)` and `challengeHeadline(inputs.challenge, timeline)`. Then try to call each one from ControllerSections and ChallengeSections using only the props NodeDetail passes today, and run `npm run build`. If any call needs data those props don't carry (it will for the handoff wait and the challenge span), widen the panels ownership to NodeDetail.tsx instead of letting the worker re-fetch inside the sections.
